title: audit-event-canonicalizer-and-compact-diff-spec-for-admin-actions
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a canonical audit event envelope and a compact, storage-friendly diffencoding for admin and RBAC v2 operations. Purpose: ensure events are actionable for incident investigation, policy auditing, and alerting while minimizing storage and index cost. Scope: events produced by SSO/SAML flows that trigger role changes, policy edits, token/key rotations, migration/upgrade admin actions, and console-admin operations.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical event envelope spec (fields, types, indexing hints) is reviewed and merged to confluence
A compact diff encoding for attribute-level changes is defined with examples for add/replace/remove
Redaction and hashing rules for PII/credentials documented and automated in ingest pipeline
Event size budget and retention/sampling guidelines established with storage impact estimates
SDK/agent change PR created with tests that emit new envelope and diff format
Console and observability dashboards updated to decode and render diffs for admin actions
technical_notes:
Canonical envelope (flat fields preferred for fast indexing): id, timestamp, source, environment, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, actor_principal, actor_authn_method, action, outcome, target_id, target_type, resource_kind, resource_id, diff_ops, snapshot_before_hash, snapshot_after_hash, event_context, request_id, trace_id.

Diff encoding: adopt a compact operation array where each op is a 3-tuple encoded as a short string: <op>|<path>|<value-or-hash>. Ops supported: A=add, R=replace, D=delete. Example: "A|roles[+]|"org-admin"", "R|policy.rules[3].allow|true", "D|service_accounts[5]||". Values that are large objects are replaced by their content-hash with a content-address map stored separately for forensic retrieval.

Indexing: index actor_id, action, target_type, resource_id, timestamp. Avoid indexing full diff contents; instead index diff-tags derived from ops (e.g., role_change, policy_rule_added, key_rotate).

Redaction: emails and usernames are stored as deterministic HMAC_SHA256 hashes with per-tenant salt. Secrets, keys, and tokens are never logged in clear; log only key_id and rotation_event=true.

Transport: events emitted from agents are batched and compressed. Storage writers must validate schema and compute snapshot hashes (sha256 of canonical stable serialization).

Backcompat: accept both legacy 'changes' array and new 'diff_ops' during transition with adapter in ingestion layer.
decisions: Use compact triplet op encoding (A|path|value-or-hash) instead of full JSON Patch to reduce event size
Keep canonical envelope flat to favor search index performance vs nested object readability
Deterministic HMAC for identity fields to allow joins without exposing PII
Store full large object payloads separately by content-hash to support replay and forensic fetch
Require security review for any change that alters redaction or hashing parameters
work_log: 2026-03-10: Spike completed comparing JSON Patch, JSON Merge Patch, and compact triplet encoding; triplet wins for size
2026-03-11: Prototype ingest adapter implemented (ingest-adapter#PR-182) and validated with 10k simulated admin events
2026-03-12: Privacy team reviewed HMAC approach; requested per-tenant salt rotation docs
2026-03-13: Ops ran storage estimate: projected 62% event size reduction vs current payloads with diff_ops and external large-object store
2026-03-14: Design review with PM/Console (notes linked) — agreed to add diff-tags for indexing and dashboard decoding helpers
notes_for_qa: QA should validate: 1) emitted events conform to envelope and diff_ops examples; 2) redacted fields are HMAC hashed and reversible only via secure forensic path; 3) index tags are populated enabling search queries for role changes and key rotations; 4) event replay from large-object store reconstructs full pre/post snapshots.
open_questions: Should we include a compact numeric enum for action types to save space (cost vs human readability)?
What SLAs do we place on forensic large-object retrieval (24h allowed?)
How do we version the diff_ops schema to support future op types?
